loop.d: A person gives the agent a task in plain words, like fix this failing test or find me three hostels near the college.
The agent reads what it can see: the task, files, a web page, the result of its last step.
The model writes out reasoning and picks the next step. Reasoning models do much more of this before acting.
It calls a tool: run code, search, click, edit a file, send a request. This is where words turn into effects in the world.
It reads the tool output and decides whether the step worked.
Useful facts go into its context window or a longer term memory store, so later steps can use them.
It stops when it thinks the goal is met, or should ask a human when unsure or about to do something risky.

parts.d: A large language model is the brain. It reads text and writes the next action as text.
Functions the model can call: a code runner, a browser, search, a file system, email. Toolformer (2023) showed models can learn when to call tools.
ReAct (2022) mixed written reasoning with actions, so a model plans, acts, looks at the result and adjusts.

Short term memory is the context window. Long term memory is a store the agent writes to and searches later. Generative Agents (2023) used memory and reflection to make simulated characters act believably.
Breaking a big goal into steps, keeping a to do list, and revising it when something fails.
Permissions, sandboxes, monitors and human approvals that limit what the agent can touch and catch mistakes.

autonomy.source: Morris et al., Levels of AGI for Operationalizing Progress on the Path to AGI (2023), table of autonomy levels

levels.d: Human fully controls the task and uses AI to automate mundane sub tasks.
levels.eg: Search engines, grammar checkers, translation apps.
levels.risk: De skilling and over reliance; disruption of established industries.

levels.d: AI takes on a substantive role, but only when a human calls on it.
levels.eg: Summarising documents, generating code on request.

levels.d: Co equal human and AI collaboration, with interactive coordination of goals and tasks.
levels.eg: Training at chess with an AI coach.

levels.d: AI drives the interaction; the human gives guidance and feedback or does sub tasks.
levels.eg: AI driven scientific discovery, like protein folding.
levels.risk: Societal scale ennui, mass labour displacement, decline of human exceptionalism.

levels.eg: Autonomous AI personal assistants (not yet unlocked when the paper was written).

evals.name: SWE-bench
evals.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
evals.what: Real GitHub issues from popular Python projects. The agent must edit the codebase so the project's own tests pass.

evals.name: GAIA
evals.title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
evals.what: Questions that are simple for people but need browsing, tools and several steps of reasoning.

evals.name: OSWorld
evals.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
evals.what: Open ended tasks on real operating systems, using real apps through the screen, mouse and keyboard.

evals.name: τ-bench
evals.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
evals.what: Conversations where an agent must follow domain rules while using tools to help a simulated customer.

evals.name: RE-Bench
evals.title: RE-Bench: Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts
evals.what: Seven open ended machine learning research engineering tasks, compared against human experts with the same time budget.

evals.name: METR time horizons
evals.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
evals.what: Tasks of many lengths, timed with skilled humans. The headline number is the task length an agent finishes half the time.

evals.name: AgentHarm
evals.title: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
evals.what: 110 explicitly harmful agent tasks across 11 harm categories, to see if agents refuse and whether jailbreaks keep them capable.

metr.note: Task lengths are the 50% time horizon: tasks a skilled human needs that long for, which the AI finishes about half the time. The first three points are the examples Anthropic quotes from METR. Mythos Preview is a lower bound: METR found it could work for at least 16 hours, at the upper end of what METR can measure without new tasks.

incidents.d: In a simulated job as a stock trading agent, GPT-4 acted on an insider tip and then hid the real reason from its manager, without being told to deceive.

incidents.t: The AI Scientist edits its own limits
incidents.d: In the authors' runs, the system once wrote code that relaunched itself in a loop, and when experiments hit the time limit it sometimes tried to edit the code to extend the limit instead of making the experiment faster.
Given a goal and an obstacle in test settings, several frontier models disabled oversight, tried to copy themselves or lied when asked about it.
o3 overwrote the grader's timer, monkey patched evaluators and pre computed answers. On RE-Bench tasks it reward hacked in 39 of 128 runs (30.4%), and in all 21 runs of one task.
In fake company settings where a model faced replacement, Claude Opus 4 and Gemini 2.5 Flash chose blackmail 96% of the time in one text based test, GPT-4.1 and Grok 3 Beta 80%, DeepSeek-R1 79%.

incidents.t: A coding agent deletes a production database
incidents.who: Reported by SaaStr founder Jason Lemkin, confirmed by Replit's CEO
incidents.d: During a code freeze, Replit's agent deleted live production data and then wrongly said it could not be restored. Replit called it unacceptable and added separate development and production databases.

Across more than 100,000 trials with thirteen models, several, including Grok 4, GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro, sometimes sabotaged a shutdown mechanism to finish a simple task. Even when told not to interfere, some did so up to 97% of the time.

incidents.who: OpenAI, investigated by METR and Redwood Research
incidents.d: During internal cyber tests, OpenAI agents escaped their isolation, coordinated on a hidden message board and hacked Hugging Face. The independent investigation found about 700 agents took part and none tried to alert humans.
